system.name: Abacus
system.one_liner: a framework that refines type-states to model hardware-software concurrency and statically prevents device drivers from violating hardware protocols

content.subject: how CPU writes to RESET, DATA and CONFIG plus hardware queue events drive UART states between Idle, Busy and QueueFull

elements.name: Reset
elements.role: write-only register; writing any value immediately empties the transmit queue and returns to Idle from any state

elements.name: Config
elements.role: read-write register holding the BAUD rate; must only be accessed while the device is Idle

elements.name: QueueReady
elements.role: superstate covering normal CPU/HW operation, refined into Idle and Busy substates

elements.name: Idle
elements.role: substate of QueueReady where the transmit queue is empty and CONFIG may legally be accessed

elements.name: Busy
elements.role: substate of QueueReady where at least one byte is queued or being transmitted

elements.name: QueueFull
elements.role: state entered when the transmit queue reaches capacity and can accept no more data

elements.name: STATUS::FULL
elements.role: hardware-evaluated flag checked after a byte is enqueued, branching to Busy (0) or QueueFull (1)

relations.what: write to RESET may happen from any state and forces the device back to Idle, emptying the queue
access CONFIG is only legal while Idle and does not change state
write to DATA (from Idle or Busy) adds a byte to the transmit queue
STATUS::FULL = 0: the queue accepted the byte and is not yet full
STATUS::FULL = 1: the queue is now full
byte transmitted: hardware drains one byte, leaving the queue non-full
last byte transmitted: the queue is now empty

transitions.guard: CPU access to CONFIG (legal only while Idle)
CPU write to DATA, then HW reports STATUS::FULL = 0
CPU write to DATA, then HW reports STATUS::FULL = 1

decisions.question: after a DATA write, does STATUS read FULL?

content.key_idea: A CPU-triggered write to DATA is checked by hardware against STATUS::FULL to decide whether the queue moves to Busy or QueueFull; RESET forces Idle from anywhere, and CONFIG may only be touched while Idle.
content.reading_order: Top panel for register bit-fields, then bottom: enter at Idle, follow solid CPU arrows up through the STATUS::FULL diamond, and dashed HW arrows back down through QueueFull to Idle.

palette.used_for: solid CPU-triggered transition arrows and the 'CPU' legend text
dashed hardware-triggered transition arrows, the STATUS::FULL diamond, and the 'HW' legend text
pale cyan background of panel (a), the register specifications
pale peach background of panel (b), the state-machine model
fill of the small CPU/HW legend box inside panel (b)

style.stroke: solid rounded-corner borders for main states, dotted rounded borders for nested substates
style.font: serif (Linux Libertine / Times Italic) for prose and italic transition labels; monospace/small-caps for register and state identifiers
style.arrows: solid arrows for CPU-triggered transitions, dashed arrows for hardware-triggered transitions, with a diamond decision node for the STATUS::FULL branch
style.icons: a diamond decision shape and a double-chevron 'from any' merge symbol; no pictorial icons

encoding.color_means: blue = a CPU-initiated action (register write/access); purple/magenta = a hardware-initiated event or the resulting HW-determined branch; the two panels' pale background tints just separate the register spec from the state model
encoding.line_style_means: solid arrows are CPU-triggered transitions; dashed arrows are hardware-triggered transitions or hardware status events
encoding.state_means: states are rounded solid-border boxes (QueueReady, QueueFull); substates are dotted-border boxes nested inside their superstate (Idle, Busy inside QueueReady)
encoding.marker_means: 0/1 on the diamond's two exits are the two possible values of the STATUS::FULL hardware flag, not step numbers
encoding.emphasis: colour alone (not position) tells the reader whether a transition is something the driver does or something the hardware does on its own, the paper's central concurrency concern
reusable_patterns: a two-colour solid/dashed arrow convention distinguishing software-triggered from hardware-triggered transitions
a nested dotted substate box inside a solid superstate box to show refinement without adding a new top-level state
a small legend box inside the diagram itself explaining the arrow-colour convention
weaknesses: panel (a)'s register bit-fields and panel (b)'s state machine are not explicitly linked by arrows or shared numbering, so the reader must match register names (RESET, CONFIG, DATA) to transitions by name only
the decision diamond's 0/1 labels require reading the STATUS register semantics from the surrounding text

evidence: we add the Reset capability proposed earlier to cancel active transactions
We also add a configuration register for the baud rate (transmission speed)
we update the model to add Idle and Busy substates to the QueueReady state

summary: Figure 2 extends the UART running example from Figure 1 with two manufacturer registers and the resulting developer state model. Panel (a) documents Reset, a write-only register that empties the transmit queue and returns to Idle from any state, and Config, a read-write baud-rate register that must only be touched while the device is Idle. Panel (b) shows the type-state model integrating both: QueueReady is refined into Idle and Busy substates so the Config restriction can be expressed, while a write to Data is followed by a hardware-evaluated STATUS::FULL check that branches to Busy or to a separate QueueFull state. Solid blue arrows mark CPU-triggered transitions (write to Reset, Data, or access Config); dashed purple arrows mark hardware-triggered transitions (STATUS::FULL becoming set, a byte transmitted, or the last byte transmitted), visually separating driver actions from hardware's own concurrent behaviour.
summary_zh: 图2扩展UART示例：Reset写入即清空队列回Idle；Config仅Idle时可访问。状态机把QueueReady分为Idle/Busy，写DATA后按队列是否已满转Busy或QueueFull，蓝实线为CPU触发，紫虚线为硬件触发。
notes: Kept the state named 'QueueFull' as literally drawn; the paper text notes it is renamed to 'QueueMaybeFull' only in a later figure (2b in a subsequent revision discussed on p.7), so it is not relabelled here.
